career.run.estimates: These rules are estimates, not measured facts. A driver may retire from age {driverFrom} and always retires at {driverCertain}. Staff may retire from age {staffFrom} and always retire at {staffCertain}. The chance on a birthday rises in equal steps from the first of those ages and is certain at the second. A scheduled driver enters the talent pool on {entryDate} of the scheduled year. Each later season fictional drivers top the pool up to {poolTarget}. A contract ending is recorded and is not renegotiated.

career.run.economy: Economy at the end of the run (estimates; start money, prize money and race running costs are booked from results, not from a January placeholder): {books} teams with books, {insolvent} insolvent, cash from {low} to {high} dollars; {deals} sponsor deals; {boards} boards, {dismissals} dismissals; {cars} cars.

pool.estimates: The pool rules are uncalibrated estimates, not facts. Each season on {entryDate} fictional drivers top the pool up to {target}. A driver without a contract leaves the pool after {maxSeasons} seasons, or once he is older than {maxAge}. Each season a member closes about {rate} percent of the gap to his hidden potential, scaled by luck between {luckMin} and {luckMax} percent. A funded junior season runs at {cheapSpeed} percent (cheap, slow) or {fastSpeed} percent (expensive, fast) of that rate.
scouting.estimates: Scouting rules are uncalibrated estimates, not facts. A band starts about {startWidth} points wide on each side and narrows with observation: time, the scout's contact network and shared races. A scout's judgement decides how far off an observation can be: a good scout never misses the true value, a poor one sometimes does. Observation alone never gives an exact value.
